## Framing

The Down syndrome data on words understood and words spoken come from the same children, on the same occasions, on overlapping vocabulary checklists. Modelling them jointly captures the relationship between the two outcomes — specifically, the production ratio `q = p_S / p_U` — that the univariate models [VG01](vg01.qmd) and [VG02](vg02.qmd) cannot represent. The production–comprehension gap in Down syndrome is the headline developmental question of this report, and the joint family (VG05, VG07, VG08, VG09) is the model family that answers it.

VG05 is the first model in this joint family. It is structurally simpler than VG07–VG09 (no random intercepts) and therefore exhibits artefacts that the random-intercept models do not. Two such artefacts surface in the VG05 posterior: the **leftward hook** in the understood-vs-spoken plot (the median understood trajectory dips between roughly 40 and 60 months while the spoken trajectory continues to rise), and the **influence-by-observation-density** problem (multi-observation subjects exert disproportionate influence on the pooled mean trajectory).

## Model specification

VG05 instantiates the joint understood-and-spoken model from the [methods chapter](methods.qmd) with `n_trials = 800` and slope anchors $(24, 84)$ months on the understood trajectory. The production-ratio reparameterisation $p_S(z) = p_U(z) \cdot q(z)$ enforces $p_S \leq p_U$ by construction.

### Slope-anchor priors

For the understood trajectory:

$$p_{24}^U \sim \mathrm{Beta}(1, 10), \qquad p_{84}^U \sim \mathrm{Beta}(1.1, 1.1).$$

For the production ratio at the same anchor ages, family-wide defaults are used:

$$p_{24}^q \sim \mathrm{Beta}(1, 1.5), \qquad p_{84}^q \sim \mathrm{Beta}(2, 1.2).$$

These centre prior mass on the production ratio being well below 1 at 24 months and approaching but not reaching 1 at 84 months — consistent with the expected receptive-productive asymmetry across the DS age range.

## Results

### Diagnostics

VG05 sampled at rep quality: r̂_max = 1.001, ESS_bulk_min = 10 362 across reported parameters (ESS_bulk_max = 54 663), zero divergences, 24 m 11 s wall time. elpd_loo = −8 830.3 (n = 1 653 observations).

### The leftward hook

The median understood trajectory shows the same 40–60-month dip identified in [VG02](vg02.qmd) (the bivariate coupling does not introduce or hide the dip — see the comparison in `notes/202604121055-understood-ds-decline.md`):

| Age (months) | Ey_median (understood) | Ey_hdi_lo | Ey_hdi_hi |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 36 | 259 | 241 | 277 |
| 42 | 290 | 269 | 311 |
| 48 | 284 | 260 | 309 |
| 54 | 273 | 245 | 303 |
| 60 | 285 | 254 | 316 |
| 66 | 330 | 294 | 365 |

In the understood-vs-spoken plot this appears as a "leftward hook" — the median trajectory's understood coordinate retreats while the spoken coordinate continues to rise, producing a non-monotonic curve that is developmentally implausible. The same artefact is what motivates VG07. See the [Simpson's-paradox section of the model comparison chapter](model-comparison.qmd#sec-simpsons-paradox) for the full diagnosis.

### Production ratio over age

| Age (months) | Spoken (median) | Production ratio (q) |
| ---: | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | – | 0.09 |
| 24 | – | 0.20 |
| 36 | – | 0.36 |
| 48 | – | 0.65 |
| 60 | – | 0.78 |
| 72 | – | 0.80 |
| 90 | – | 0.88 |

The headline numbers under VG05 broadly resemble those under VG07, but the absence of study-level random intercepts means the trajectory tracks observation density rather than child frequency. This is the second of the two artefacts that motivate the random-intercept extensions.

The full posterior summary tables (`posterior_summary_u.csv`, `posterior_summary_s.csv`, `posterior_summary_q.csv`) and figures are in `output/models/VG05-age-understood-spoken-ds/`. The rendered per-model report is `output/models/VG05-age-understood-spoken-ds/index.html`.

## Status of VG05 in the family

VG05 has been superseded for reporting headline DS joint numbers by VG07 → VG08 → VG09. Its place in this report is methodological: it is the simplest joint model and the model whose two surfaced artefacts (the leftward hook and the observation-density bias) motivate the entire random-intercept family.

## Limitations

- **No study-level structure.** Between-study differences in measurement and reporting are absorbed into the Beta-Binomial dispersion and the GP departure rather than into a structural term. VG07 partitions them out explicitly.
- **No subject-level structure.** Multi-observation subjects (288 of 510 DS subjects) exert disproportionate influence on the pooled trajectory. VG08 and VG09 partition this out.
- **The leftward-hook artefact.** Quoted understood numbers in the 40–60-month range under VG05 should not be read at face value. The corresponding numbers under VG07–VG09 are the ones to cite.
